body:
# the contributor audit of local signed mass changes and the compatibility obstruction

Source: `candidate 97eab0f821e54041`.
Result: **PASS under its explicit hypotheses**. No unrestricted
localization assertion is inferred.

Strict compatibility is tested on finitely many extreme anchored
representations. Convex combinations and support functions extend the
same uniform margin to every representation; cancellation of a target's
own coefficient is legitimate. Independent Hausdorff perturbations of
size less than half that margin therefore remain actual fibers.

The outward locality proof uses both unique supporting normal and
singleton contact face. Compactness first forces visible normals to
the unique normal, and then forces the other endpoint of each exterior
convex combination to the singleton face. The nested hulls have strictly
different support values and positive volume differences, justifying
the exact continuous mass inverse. For finitely many distinct points,
their visible-normal sets are disjoint for sufficiently small bumps.
An exterior support face of the combined hull can then contain only
one added point, and the radial segment from an interior point proves
the claimed exact union of the individual exterior regions.

Global exposure supplies a strict gap to all other integer fibers and
all other selected points. Thus the inward cuts remove only their
prescribed original local regions and do not touch the outward bumps.
The signs and total mass identity are exact. Fixed nonzero cap margins
also preserve every incidence under threshold movements of order
epsilon. These are the points where the exposure, finiteness, and
boundary-avoidance assumptions are essential.

The threshold shifts in the variational proof have exactly zero
rho-weighted sum, so they cover each entire candidate plane, including
new points in enlarged fibers. Equal positive left and right slopes
give the asserted first-order cap masses. Nondeep bases retain fixed
slack. Dividing by the exact new total gives the stated upper derivative
bound. Separation of finitely many row vectors proves the equality
dual for the one fixed selection of points and circuits; it does not
create a selection-independent multiplier.

In the ball-cylinder obstruction the three displayed sections are
exact Minkowski combinations. Brunn--Minkowski and the elementary
power expansion give Delta_1>=2^(-d)Delta_0, while inclusion gives
Delta_1<=Delta_0. The lost locality concerns a positive fraction of
added mass at lattice distance at least one. In the plane, the tangent
triangle-minus-circle-cap area equals s-theta, and the perimeter excess
equals twice this quantity. The parallel-body area formula therefore
gives exactly Delta_1=3Delta_0/4 and nonlocal fraction 3/7. Binary
padding preserves these sections and the asserted absence of a heavy
fiber. The example refutes the proposed auxiliary localization without
strict compatibility; it does not refute OC.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
